CHARLOTTE, NC / ACCESS Newswire / November 13, 2026 / Air T, Inc. (NASDAQ:AIRT) is an industrious American company with a portfolio of businesses, each of which is independent yet interrelated. We seek dynamic individuals and teams to operate companies with processes and insights that drive increasing value over time. We believe we can invest corporate resources to help activate growth and overcome challenges.

Our core segments are regional airline, overnight air cargo; commercial aircraft, engines and parts; ground support equipment; digital solutions; and aviation leasing and asset management.

Today, Air T announced results for the fiscal second quarter ended September 30, 2026:

  • Revenues totaled $146.9 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $82.8 million, or 129% from the prior year's comparable quarter. Revenues for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 included $56.8 million related to our acquisition of Regional Express Holdings Pty Ltd ("Rex") completed on December 18, 2025.
  • Operating loss was $11.8 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to the prior year's comparable quarter's operating income of $5.5 million.
  • Loss before income taxes was $16.2 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to income before income taxes of $7.2 million in the prior year's comparable quarter.
  • Adjusted EBITDA* was $4.4 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $7.9 million in the prior year's comparable quarter.
  • The investment balance for the Company's equity method investees was $26.2 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $27.9 million at September 30, 2025.
  • Net loss per share was $7.48 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to net income per share of $1.61 in the prior year's comparable quarter.

*Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP financial measure; see below for further explanation and reconciliation to GAAP measure.

Company Chairman and CEO Nick Swenson commented:

"While focused in one sector and with some interdependencies, Air T can be viewed as a set of businesses that operate independently of one another. The quarter just passed is an example of widely variable operational dynamics across our businesses. Several of our businesses, including Crestone and GGS, performed quite well in absolute terms and against comparables in the quarter. Crestone has particularly strong momentum at the moment. Rex financial performance was notably challenged in the quarter due to a combination of unscheduled engine removals, delays at engine overhaul shops and a doubling of fuel costs compared to pre-war levels. Adding back the large quarterly depreciation expense at Rex, we see an Adjusted EBITDA loss of approximately $0.9 million on $56.8 million of revenues for the quarter. Management continues to support business leaders as they navigate areas of risk management and growth management."

Business Segment Results

Regional Airline

  • This segment provides scheduled regional passenger and cargo airline services in Australia, operating a fleet of aircraft serving regional communities and connecting passengers to major metropolitan centers.
  • Revenues for this segment were $56.8 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, representing a full quarter of Rex operations, which was acquired on December 18, 2025. There is no prior-year comparable. Revenue consisted of passenger revenue, ancillary fees, freight and charter, and government subsidy income.
  • Adjusted EBITDA* loss for this segment was $0.9 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. The significant add-backs to this segment's operating loss of $10.0 million include $9.4 million of depreciation and amortization. Fuel expense continued to be the primary driver of the loss, with the increase driven principally by higher per-liter fuel prices rather than increased consumption. Rex does not hedge its fuel price or related Australian dollar/U.S. dollar exposure and purchases fuel at prevailing market prices, mitigating higher costs through fare adjustments, capacity management, and fuel levy arrangements with certain state governments. Higher unscheduled engine removals, together with lower engine throughput from third-party maintenance, repair and overhaul providers, also contributed to the loss by reducing the number of aircraft available for service below planned levels.

Overnight Air Cargo

  • This segment provides air express delivery services, primarily for FedEx Corporation, and repair services.
  • Revenues for this segment totaled $34.5 million period ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $3.5 million compared to the second quarter of the prior fiscal year. The increase was principally attributable to higher pricing on flight administrative fees and billable labor at Mountain Air Cargo ("MAC").
  • Adjusted EBITDA* for this segment was $2.6 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $0.8 million when compared to the prior year's comparable quarter. The increase was mainly driven by higher revenue. In addition, higher gross margins related to both flight operations and maintenance at MAC drove operating income and Adjusted EBITDA higher.

Commercial Aircraft, Engines and Parts

  • This segment acquires, leases, manages, repairs, disassembles, and sells commercial aircraft, jet engines, and aviation components, and provides related asset management, procurement, overhaul, repair, and logistics services.
  • Revenues for this segment totaled $28.5 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $7.0 million from the comparable prior year quarter. The increase was largely attributable to increased component sales at Contrail, primarily driven by an increase in sales to a single customer. Landing Gear Support Services, Inc. ("LGSS") and AirCo also contributed to the revenue growth due to strategic investments in aircraft inventory that were not in place during the prior year comparable quarter. Jet Yard saw reduced revenue, primarily due to the prior year quarter's revenue including some larger projects that did not recur in the current quarter.
  • Adjusted EBITDA* for this segment was $1.5 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to adjusted EBITDA* of $6.9 million in the prior year's comparable quarter. The decrease was primarily attributable to a $7.0 million gain on sale of aircraft in the prior year quarter, which did not recur in the current quarter. Partially offsetting the impact of this transaction was the overall revenue increase in this segment.

Ground Support Equipment

  • This segment-which includes some of the world-leading offerings in the category-manufactures, repairs, and maintains mobile deicers and other specialized ground-support equipment. Customers include passenger and cargo airlines, airports, the military, and other industrial customers.
  • Revenues for this segment totaled $18.9 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $9.2 million from $9.6 million in the prior year's comparable quarter. The increase was primarily driven by a higher number of deicing trucks sold in the current quarter as a result of timing on fulfilling annual orders for a large customer.
  • Adjusted EBITDA* for this segment was $2.7 million in the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to adjusted EBITDA* of $1.7 million in the prior year's comparable quarter. The increase was primarily attributable to the higher sales from timing of revenues as noted above.
  • At September 30, 2026, this segment's order backlog was $11.6 million compared to $12.9 million at September 30, 2025.

Digital Solutions

  • This segment develops and provides digital aviation and other business services to customers within the aviation industry to generate recurring subscription revenues.
  • The digital solutions segment contributed $2.6 million of revenues for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $2.2 million in the prior year's comparable quarter. The increase of $0.4 million was primarily due to continued growth in data analytics and airspace management engagements.
  • Adjusted EBITDA* for this segment was $0.1 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $0.2 million from the prior year's comparable quarter. The improvement was primarily driven by two factors: revenue growth at high incremental margins and lower labor costs as AI-driven tools improved efficiency.

Aviation Leasing and Asset Management

  • This segment originates and structures asset acquisitions and related financings and provides lease administration, technical and risk management, and remarketing services for aircraft and engines on lease to airline customers globally.
  • The aviation leasing and asset management segment revenues totaled $7.8 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, representing a full quarter of activity for Crestone and Arena, which made up the segment as of the acquisition of Arena on June 10, 2026. There is no prior year comparable quarter. Revenue consisted of origination, due diligence, disposition, and asset management fees.
  • Adjusted EBITDA* for this segment was $1.3 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, representing a full quarter of operations after the Arena acquisition and quarter-to-date activity related to Crestone Air Partners. The largest reconciling items between Adjusted EBITDA and this segment's operating loss of $4.7 million include an unfavorable earnout remeasurement of $3.3 million, depreciation and amortization add-backs of $2.2 million, and post-acquisition integration costs of $0.5 million.

*Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP financial measure; see below for further explanation and reconciliation to GAAP measures.

Non-GAAP Financial Measures

The Company uses Adjusted EBITDA, a non-GAAP financial measure, to evaluate the Company's financial performance. The Company defines Adjusted EBITDA as operating income (loss), adjusted for the items shown in the reconciliation below.

Management believes that Adjusted EBITDA is a useful measure of the Company's performance because it provides investors additional information about the Company's operations allowing better evaluation of underlying business performance and better period-to-period comparability. We may periodically review and update our non-GAAP financial measures based on our determination of their relevance to our business which could result in the addition or elimination of select non-GAAP financial measures in the future. Adjusted EBITDA is not intended to replace or be an alternative to operating (loss) income, the most directly comparable GAAP measure.

NOTE REGARDING STAKEHOLDER QUESTIONS

If you have questions related to this release or other Air T matters, please use our interactive Q&A capability, through Slido.com, accessible from our website, to submit your questions. We intend to keep that link open and available for shareholder questions. ABOUT AIR T, INC.

Established in 1980, Air T, Inc. is a portfolio of powerful businesses and financial assets, each of which is independent yet interrelated. Its core segments are overnight air cargo, ground support equipment, commercial aircraft, engines and parts, regional airline, digital solutions, and aviation leasing and asset management. We seek to expand, strengthen and diversify Air T's after-tax cash flow per share. Our goal is to build Air T's core businesses, and when appropriate, to expand into adjacent and other industries. LOS ANGELES, Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- XMax Inc. (NASDAQ: XMAX, “XMAX” or the “Company”), a distributor of contemporary furniture and artificial intelligence software and platform-based service provider, today announced financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights

  • Revenue: $6.4 million, down 34% from $9.8 million in the third quarter of 2025, including $4.5 million from API-based services and $1.9 million from furniture (down 81%, as the prior-year period included a $7.9 million marble slab liquidation sale)
  • Gross Profit: $0.9 million, representing a 14% gross margin, compared to gross profit of $1.0 million and gross margin of 10% for the third quarter of 2025
  • Net Loss: $(9.0) million, driven primarily by a $10.5 million non-cash unrealized loss on the Company's investment in Preamble Capital and partially offset by a $3.6 million deferred tax benefit, compared to a net loss of $(1.1) million in the third quarter of 2025
  • Cash and Cash Equivalents: $10.6 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to $6.7 million at December 31, 2025
  • Working Capital: $22.0 million as of September 30, 2026, up from $9.4 million at December 31, 2025

Management Commentary

“The third quarter of 2026 was a period of rapid scaling for XMax as our API-based services generated $4.5 million of revenue, their first full quarter of contribution,” said Xiaohua Lu, Chief Executive Officer of the Company. “We reported a net loss of $9.0 million for the quarter, driven primarily by a $10.5 million non-cash unrealized loss on our investment in Preamble Capital, partly offset by a $3.6 million deferred tax benefit. For the first nine months, net income was $23.6 million, while our balance sheet was supported by approximately $10.6 million in cash, $22.0 million in working capital and a $79.3 million investment in Preamble Capital funds as of September 30, 2026.”

“Our overall gross margin was 14% in the third quarter, compared to 10% a year ago, when results included a low-margin marble slab liquidation sale. Furniture gross margin was 51%, while our API-based services were approximately break-even at the gross level as we scale,” Mr. Lu continued. “Total revenue declined 34% to $6.4 million as furniture sales fell 81% to $1.9 million, reflecting the prior-year liquidation sale, challenging market conditions and tariffs, only partly offset by $4.5 million from our API-based services. With working capital of $22.0 million, up from $9.4 million at year-end, we have financial flexibility to pursue our strategic AI initiatives.”

“Looking ahead, our priority is to scale our AI offerings through XMax AI Inc. in the U.S. and Elonx AI Holdings PTE. LTD. in Singapore, while allocating capital with discipline to build long-term value for our shareholders,” Mr. Lu added. “In October, we signed an agreement for dedicated NVIDIA B300 GPU capacity of up to 512 GPUs, subject to closing conditions. Combined with our live API platform, this would meaningfully expand the compute we can offer enterprise customers building AI into their products and operations.”

“We are also committed to returning value to shareholders,” Mr. Lu added. “In October, our Board authorized a share repurchase program of up to $30 million, to be funded from existing cash and shares shall be repurchased at prices below $5.50 per share and the Company has commenced repurchases of its common stock on November 5, 2026 through its engaged broker-dealer with purchases made from time to time in the open market in accordance with Rule 10b-18.”

About XMax Inc.

Headquartered in Commerce, California, XMax Inc. (NASDAQ: XMAX), formerly known as Nova LifeStyle, Inc., is a diversified company engaged in the design, sourcing, and distribution of contemporary furniture, as well as the development of artificial intelligence technologies and applications. The Company operates through an established global network of suppliers, distributors, and e-commerce channels, serving a broad customer base. In addition, the Company is expanding into artificial intelligence technologies, including AI software and platform-based services through its wholly owned subsidiaries XMax AI Inc. and Elonx AI Holdings PTE. LTD., to support future growth. By leveraging emerging technologies, the Company aims to drive diversification and long-term value creation.

Key Terms

restricted stock unitsfinancial
Restricted stock units are a type of company reward where employees are promised shares of stock, but they only fully own these shares after meeting certain conditions, like staying with the company for a set time. They matter because they can become valuable assets and are often used to motivate employees to help the company succeed.
nasdaq listing rule 5635(c)(4)regulatory
NASDAQ Listing Rule 5635(c)(4) is a rule that requires a company to get approval from its shareholders before selling a large amount of its shares, usually over 20%. This helps protect investors by making sure the company doesn't flood the market with new shares without their say, which could lower the stock's value.
spinal muscular atrophymedical
A genetic condition in which the “wiring” between the spinal cord and muscles fails, causing progressive loss of muscle strength and motor skills from infancy through adulthood as the nerve cells that move muscles deteriorate. Investors pay attention because the condition creates a clear, long-term need for specialized therapies, diagnostics and ongoing care — meaning successful drugs or tests can attract premium pricing, sustained demand and significant regulatory and reimbursement scrutiny that materially affect biotech and healthcare valuations.
smn2medical
SMN2 is a human gene that acts like a weaker backup copy of the main SMN gene responsible for producing a protein vital to motor nerve cell survival. For investors, SMN2 matters because the number and behavior of its copies affect disease severity and are a key target for diagnostics and therapies; treatments that boost its output can change patient outcomes, regulatory paths, and commercial value in the biotech market.
monoclonal antibodiesmedical
Monoclonal antibodies are lab-made proteins designed to bind a single, specific target on cells or viruses, like identical keys cut to fit one lock. They are used as medicines, tests, or targeted delivery tools and can precisely block or mark disease processes. Investors care because they can become high-value drugs with large sales, long patent protection, and binary risks tied to clinical trial results, regulatory approval, manufacturing scale and pricing.

BOSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Eastern Bankshares, Inc. (the “Company”) (Nasdaq: EBC), the holding company of Eastern Bank, today announced its Board of Directors (the “Board”) has unanimously elected Peter K. Markell as Lead Independent Director, effective January 1, 2027. Mr. Markell will succeed Deborah C. Jackson, who will step down as Lead Director effective January 1, 2027, in anticipation of her planned retirement from the Board at year-end 2027. The Company also announced Director and Chair Emeritus Richard E. Holbrook will retire from the Board effective December 31, 2026 in accordance with the mandatory age limitations for members of the Board set forth in the Company’s Corporate Governance Guidelines, and Luis A. Borgen will resign from the Board effective December 31, 2026 to devote more time to his personal and professional commitments.

Lead Independent Director Transition
Mr. Markell has served as a director of the Company, and as a trustee of its predecessor holding company, Eastern Bank Corporation, since 2006. He currently chairs the Board’s Audit Committee and serves on its Risk Management Committee, and Compensation and Human Capital Management Committee. Mr. Markell was recommended for the role by the Board’s Nominating and Governance Committee and elected by the Board’s independent Directors, consistent with the Company’s Corporate Governance Guidelines.

Mr. Markell has served as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of Brown University Health (formerly Lifespan) since January 2023. Previously, he served as Executive Vice President of Administration and Finance, Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer of Mass General Brigham, which he joined in 1999, until March 2021. Prior to that, he was a partner at Ernst & Young LLP. A Certified Public Accountant, Mr. Markell is a graduate of Boston College, where he served as both Chair of the Board and Chair of its Finance Committee. He serves on the boards of directors of Huron Consulting Group Inc. and CodaMetrix.

“Peter Markell has been a trusted and steady voice on our Board for two decades, and his deep financial expertise, leadership of our Audit Committee and broad perspective across our committees make him exceptionally well suited to lead our independent directors,” said Bob Rivers, Executive Chair and Chair of the Board of Directors of Eastern Bankshares, Inc. and Eastern Bank. “We are equally grateful to Deborah Jackson, who has led our independent directors with exceptional integrity and excellence since 2018. She guided the Board through an extraordinary period of transformation, from our initial public offering through a series of mergers, and through it all she kept our mission and our commitment to the communities we serve at the center of our work, helping to solidify our role as the largest, locally-headquartered bank in Boston. We are fortunate to continue to benefit from her counsel as a director through 2027.”

Of his new Board role, Mr. Markell said, “I am honored by the confidence of my fellow directors and grateful to Deborah Jackson for the strong example she has set. Eastern is a company with a remarkable history and an even brighter future, and I look forward to working closely with Bob and my fellow directors in this new role.”

Ms. Jackson added, “For more than two centuries, Eastern has modelled what it means for a bank to lead in, and for, the communities it serves, and that commitment matters as much today as it ever has. It has been my privilege to serve on this Board for more than 25 years and as Lead Director since 2018, a period in which Eastern became a public company, grew organically and through several mergers, and never lost sight of who we serve. Peter has been a valued colleague and an exceptional Audit Committee Chair, and I have every confidence in his leadership. I look forward to supporting Peter, Bob and my fellow directors through a seamless transition, and to continuing to champion Eastern’s mission as a director through 2027.”

Director Retirement and Resignation
Mr. Holbrook will retire from the Boards of Directors of the Company and Eastern Bank effective December 31, 2026, in accordance with the mandatory age limitations for directors set forth in the Company’s Corporate Governance Guidelines. Mr. Holbrook, who has been a director of Eastern Bank since 2001, was also Chair Emeritus. He retired as Chair and CEO of Eastern Bank in 2016, having served in those roles since 2007. He served on the Risk Management Committee of the Board immediately prior to his resignation.

Mr. Borgen, who has been a director of Eastern Bank since 2016, chaired the Risk Management Committee of the Board immediately prior to his resignation. An accomplished public company finance executive, Mr. Borgen previously served as Chief Financial Officer of athenahealth, Inc., among other publicly traded companies, and served as a Captain in the U.S. Air Force.

Neither Mr. Holbrook nor Mr. Borgen is leaving the Board as the result of any disagreement with the Company on any matter relating to its operations, policies or practices.

Mr. Rivers stated, “We are very thankful for the many contributions Rich Holbrook and Luis Borgen have made to our Company. Rich joined Eastern in 1996 and since that time has strengthened our Company through his exemplary leadership and financial stewardship as CFO, CEO, Board Chair, and Director. There are few in the community banking industry who have contributed more than Rich, and we are incredibly grateful to benefit from his leadership. Luis Borgen’s decades of financial expertise and public company experience likewise strengthened our Board. We wish them both the very best in their next chapters. On behalf of my fellow directors and leadership team, I want to thank Deborah, Rich and Luis for their counsel, candor and expertise. I look forward to working with Peter and the full Board as we continue to deliver for our customers, colleagues, communities and shareholders across the communities we serve.”

About Eastern Bankshares, Inc.
Eastern Bankshares, Inc. is the holding company for Eastern Bank. Founded in 1818, Eastern Bank is Greater Boston’s leading local bank with more than 125 branch locations serving communities in eastern Massachusetts, southern and coastal New Hampshire, and Rhode Island. As of September 30, 2026, Eastern had approximately $31.7 billion in assets. Eastern provides a full range of banking and wealth management solutions for consumers and businesses of all sizes including through its Cambridge Trust Wealth Management and Private Banking Divisions, which include the largest bank-owned independent investment adviser in Massachusetts with $10.8 billion in assets under management. Eastern takes pride in its advocacy and community support that includes more than $240 million in charitable giving since 1994. An inclusive company, Eastern is comprised of deeply committed professionals who value relationships with their customers, colleagues and communities. Key Terms

form 10-qregulatory
A Form 10-Q is a detailed report that publicly traded companies are required to file with regulators three times a year, providing an update on their financial health and business activities. It is important for investors because it offers timely insights into a company's performance, helping them make informed decisions about buying or selling stocks. Think of it as a regular check-up report that shows how well a company is doing.
equity methodfinancial
An equity method investment is an accounting approach used when a company owns enough of another business to influence its decisions but not control it (commonly around 20–50% ownership). Instead of counting only dividends, the investor records its share of the other company’s profits and losses on its own income statement and adjusts the investment’s value on the balance sheet—like tracking a friend’s joint project by noting your share of their gains or setbacks. For investors, this matters because it can significantly affect reported earnings, asset values, and the apparent strength of a company’s financial results.
rule 10b5-1regulatory
Rule 10b5-1 is a regulation that allows company insiders to buy or sell their shares at predetermined times, even if they have access to non-public information. It acts like setting a schedule in advance for transactions, helping prevent accusations of unfair trading. This rule provides a way for insiders to plan trades transparently, giving investors confidence that these transactions are not based on hidden information.
fair valuefinancial
Fair value is an estimate of what an asset or company is really worth today, derived from expected future earnings, comparable market prices and other relevant facts—like agreeing a price for a used car after checking mileage, condition and similar listings. Investors use fair value to decide whether a stock looks overpriced or undervalued, which helps guide buy, hold or sell decisions and sets expectations for potential returns and risk.

NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--American Strategic Investment Co. (NYSE: NYC) (“ASIC” or the “Company”), a company that owns a portfolio of commercial real estate located within the five boroughs of New York City, announced today its financial and operating results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Highlights

  • Revenue was $7.1 million compared to $12.3 million in the third quarter of 2025, primarily related to the disposition of 1140 Avenue of the Americas in the prior year
  • Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $6.7 million, compared to net income of $35.8 million in the third quarter of 2025 that was primarily due to a non-cash gain recognized in connection with the disposition of 1140 Avenue of the Americas in the third quarter of 2025
  • Cash net operating income (“Cash NOI”) was $3.5 million, compared to $5.3 million in the third quarter of 2025
  • Adjusted EBITDA was $1.0 million, compared to $1.9 million in the third quarter of 2025
  • Weighted-average remaining lease term(1) was 6.0 years compared to 6.1 years at the end of the second quarter of 2026
  • 69% of annualized straight-line rent from top 10 tenants(2) was derived from investment grade or implied investment grade(3) rated tenants with a weighted-average remaining lease term of 6.7 years, up slightly from 6.4 years at the end of the prior quarter
  • Portfolio comprised of fixed rate debt at a 4.56% weighted-average interest rate
  • Subsequent to quarter end, signed an extension and expansion lease with the State of New York at 123 William Street extending the current lease to 2037 and adding approximately 30,000 square feet on two additional floors.

CEO Comments

“The Company’s results this quarter build on the progress we made over the last two quarters, as our capital prioritization strategy continues to contribute to our results,” said Nicholas Schorsch, Jr., CEO of ASIC. “The portfolio’s high quality, largely investment grade tenant base continues to support stable performance this year. We remain focused on completing our remaining asset dispositions and directing capital toward the opportunities we believe will create the most durable value for our shareholders, such as the execution of the lease with the State of New York after the end of the quarter that increases pro-forma occupancy at 123 William Street to approximately 75% and portfolio occupancy to approximately 78%.”

Non-GAAP Financial Measures

This release discusses the non-GAAP financial measures we use to evaluate our performance, including Earnings before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization (“EBITDA”), Adjusted Earnings before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization (“Adjusted EBITDA”), Net Operating Income (“NOI”) and Cash Net Operating Income (“Cash NOI”) and Cash Paid for Interest. A description of these non-GAAP measures and reconciliations to the most directly comparable GAAP measure, which is net loss, is provided above.

In December 2022 we announced that we changed our business strategy and terminated our election to be taxed as a REIT effective January 1, 2023, however, our business and operations have not materially changed in the third quarter of 2026. Therefore, we did not change any of the non-GAAP metrics that we have historically used to evaluate performance.

Caution on Use of Non-GAAP Measures

EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA, NOI, Cash NOI and Cash Paid for Interest should not be construed to be more relevant or accurate than the current GAAP methodology in calculating net income or in its applicability in evaluating our operating performance. The method utilized to evaluate the value and performance of real estate under GAAP should be construed as a more relevant measure of operational performance and considered more prominently than the non-GAAP metrics.

As a result, we believe that the use of these non-GAAP metrics, together with the required GAAP presentations, provide a more complete understanding of our performance, including relative to our peers and a more informed and appropriate basis on which to make decisions involving operating, financing, and investing activities. However, these non-GAAP metrics are not indicative of cash available to fund ongoing cash needs, including the ability to pay cash dividends. Investors are cautioned that these non-GAAP metrics should only be used to assess the sustainability of our operating performance excluding these activities, as they exclude certain costs that have a negative effect on our operating performance during the periods in which these costs are incurred.

Adjusted Earnings before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization, Net Operating Income, Cash Net Operating Income and Cash Paid for Interest.

We believe that EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA, which is defined as earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization adjusted for (i) impairment charges, (ii) interest income or other income or expense, (iii) gains or losses on debt extinguishment, (iv) equity-based compensation expense, (v) acquisition and transaction costs, (vi) gains or losses from the sale of real estate investments and (vii) expenses paid with issuances of common stock in lieu of cash is an appropriate measure of our ability to incur and service debt. We consider EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA useful indicators of our performance. Because these metrics’ calculations exclude such factors as depreciation and amortization of real estate assets, interest expense, and equity-based compensation (which can vary among owners of identical assets in similar conditions based on historical cost accounting and useful-life estimates), these metrics; presentations facilitate comparisons of operating performance between periods and between other companies that use these measures. Adjusted EBITDA should not be considered as an alternative to cash flows from operating activities, as a measure of our liquidity or as an alternative to net income as an indicator of our operating activities. Other companies may calculate Adjusted EBITDA differently and our calculation should not be compared to that of other companies.

NOI is a non-GAAP financial measure used by us to evaluate the operating performance of our real estate. NOI is equal to total revenues, excluding contingent purchase price consideration, less property operating and maintenance expense. NOI excludes all other items of expense and income included in the financial statements in calculating net income (loss). We believe NOI provides useful and relevant information because it reflects only those income and expense items that are incurred at the property level and presents such items on an unleveraged basis. We use NOI to assess and compare property level performance and to make decisions concerning the operations of the properties. Further, we believe NOI is useful to investors as a performance measure because, when compared across periods, NOI reflects the impact on operations from trends in occupancy rates, rental rates, operating expenses and acquisition activity on an unleveraged basis, providing perspective not immediately apparent from net income (loss). NOI excludes certain items included in calculating net income (loss) in order to provide results that are more closely related to a property’s results of operations. For example, interest expense is not necessarily linked to the operating performance of a real estate asset. In addition, depreciation and amortization, because of historical cost accounting and useful life estimates, may distort operating performance at the property level. NOI presented by us may not be comparable to NOI reported by other companies that define NOI differently. We believe that in order to facilitate a clear understanding of our operating results, NOI should be examined in conjunction with net income (loss) as presented in our consolidated financial statements. NOI should not be considered as an alternative to net income (loss) as an indication of our performance or to cash flows as a measure of our liquidity or our ability to pay dividends.

Cash NOI, is a non-GAAP financial measure that is intended to reflect the performance of our properties. We define Cash NOI as NOI excluding amortization of above/below market lease intangibles and straight-line adjustments that are included in GAAP lease revenues. We believe that Cash NOI is a helpful measure that both investors and management can use to evaluate the current financial performance of our properties and it allows for comparison of our operating performance between periods and to other companies. Cash NOI should not be considered as an alternative to net income, as an indication of our financial performance, or to cash flows as a measure of liquidity or our ability to fund all needs. The method by which we calculate and present Cash NOI may not be directly comparable to the way other companies present Cash NOI.

Cash Paid for Interest is calculated based on the interest expense less non-cash portion of interest expense and amortization of mortgage (discount) premium, net. Management believes that Cash Paid for Interest provides useful information to investors to assess our overall solvency and financial flexibility. Cash Paid for Interest should not be considered as an alternative to interest expense as determined in accordance with GAAP or any other GAAP financial measures and should only be considered together with and as a supplement to our financial information prepared in accordance with GAAP.

Key Terms

straight-line rentfinancial
An accounting method that spreads the total rent cost or rental income evenly across the full lease period, so each reporting period shows the same amount even if actual cash payments vary (for example, due to free months or stepped increases). For investors, straight-line rent matters because it smooths earnings and can hide timing differences between cash flow and reported profit, affecting measures like operating income and the apparent stability of a landlord’s or tenant’s finances—think of turning a lumpy payment schedule into a steady monthly subscription on the books.
consensual foreclosurefinancial
A consensual foreclosure is the enforcement of a lender’s security interest in collateral that the borrower agreed in advance could be seized or sold if certain contract conditions (typically a default) occur. It relies on a prior agreement—such as a mortgage, deed of trust, or security agreement—that authorizes the lender to take possession, sell the asset, or otherwise satisfy the debt, and it may proceed under a nonjudicial process specified by the contract and applicable statute or by judicial sale if required. The key distinction is that the borrower previously granted the remedy in the security instrument, so the foreclosure enforces those agreed remedies rather than arising from an unrelated court judgment against the debtor.
promissory notefinancial
A promissory note is a written IOU in which one party promises to pay a specific sum, often with interest, to another party by a set date or on demand. Investors care because it functions like a loan: it creates a legal claim on future cash flows, carries credit and timing risk, and can affect valuation or liquidity—think of it as a formal, tradable promise to be repaid that can be assessed like any other debt investment.

The Company presents an economic debt-to-equity ratio, a non-GAAP financial measure of leverage that considers the impact of the off-balance sheet financing of its investments in TBAs that are accounted for as derivative instruments under U.S. GAAP and the impact of receivables and payables for unsettled trades (if any). The Company includes these types of TBAs at implied cost basis in its measure of leverage because a forward contract to acquire Agency RMBS in the TBA market carries similar risks to Agency RMBS purchased in the cash market and funded with on-balance sheet liabilities. Similarly, a contract for the forward sale of Agency RMBS has substantially the same effect as selling the underlying Agency RMBS and reducing the Company's on-balance sheet funding commitments. The Company adjusts leverage for receivables and payables for unsettled trades (if any) because sales or purchases of MBS are recorded on the balance sheet on the trade date, while any corresponding changes to repurchase agreement borrowings are not recorded until the settlement date. Millicom (Tigo) signs agreement to acquire Entel Peru, expanding its presence across Latin America

The transaction expands Millicom’s presence in investment-grade markets and is expected to be accretive to equity free cash flow in the first year following completion. Closing is expected in early December, subject to customary closing conditions.

  

Luxembourg, November 13, 2026 – Millicom (NASDAQ: TIGO) today announced that it has signed an agreement to acquire Entel Peru for US$1,714 million, including lease liabilities, implying a transaction multiple of 5.0x estimated 2026 EBITDA, before synergies and integration costs. This transaction marks another important step in Millicom's regional growth strategy and is expected to be funded through a combination of local financing and cash on hand. The purchase price will be paid in three installments: 65% at closing, 10% twelve months after closing, and 25% eighteen months after closing. The transaction is expected to close in early December 2026, subject to satisfaction of certain closing conditions.

Upon completion, the acquisition would expand Millicom’s footprint to 13 markets and further advance its strategy of geographic diversification, increasing its presence in investment-grade economies. Peru, which holds investment-grade sovereign ratings from Moody’s, S&P and Fitch, offers a market of more than 34 million people and an attractive foundation for long-term growth in connectivity and digital services.

Entel Peru’s established network, strong postpaid customer base and enterprise relationships provide an attractive platform for profitable growth. Following completion, Millicom intends to build on these strengths by applying its operational improvement capabilities, regional purchasing power and disciplined approach to capital allocation. The Group sees significant opportunities to improve efficiency, optimize working capital and strengthen cash generation, while preserving service quality and customer experience.

The acquisition would also create opportunities to expand higher-value services for consumers and businesses. Entel Peru’s access to an extensive fiber footprint through wholesale partnerships, combined with Millicom’s experience in mobile and home connectivity, would support capital-efficient growth in convergent services, stronger customer relationships and additional recurring revenues.

Millicom expects the transaction to be accretive to equity free cash flow in its first year following completion, consistent with the approach taken in its recent Telefónica acquisitions. Despite the anticipated closing late in the year, the Group expects year-end 2026 leverage to remain around 2.5x, including the acquisition. The transaction is not expected to adversely affect planned shareholder distributions and is expected to strengthen the Group’s capacity to support distributions over time through increased cash generation.

Marcelo Benitez, CEO of Millicom, commented: “We are very excited about entering Peru, a great country with tremendous potential and an important new chapter in our growth journey across Latin America. Over the past few years, we have demonstrated our ability to successfully integrate new operations, improve customer experience and deliver strong financial results. We have a proven playbook built around our Double-E strategy: delivering the best customer Experience with the greatest Efficiency. We are confident in our ability to replicate that success in Peru. Entel Peru brings a strong network, loyal customers and a talented team. Together, we see a great opportunity to invest in connectivity, bring better services and greater value to Peruvian consumers and businesses, and contribute to the country’s digital development. Our focus remains the same: disciplined execution, profitable growth and sustainable cash flow generation. We look forward to welcoming the Entel Peru team to the Millicom family and building a successful future together.”

Peru: An attractive platform for long-term growth

  • A sizeable market with significant digital potential: With more than 34 million people, Peru offers a substantial customer base for mobile connectivity, home broadband and enterprise solutions. Millicom sees opportunities to deepen digital adoption and expand higher-value services for households and businesses.
  • A growing economy with an attractive medium-term outlook: The IMF’s October 2026 projections anticipate economic growth of 2.9% in 2027 and 3.2% in 2028, with nominal GDP reaching approximately US$414 billion in 2027. Strong macroeconomic institutions, relatively low public debt and substantial international reserves provide a supportive foundation for long-term investment.
  • Investment-grade credentials and international investor confidence: Peru holds investment-grade sovereign ratings of Baa1 from Moody’s, BBB from Fitch and BBB− from S&P. As of November 5, 2026, its J.P. Morgan sovereign bond spread stood at 121 basis points, approximately 43% below the Latin American benchmark, placing Peru among the region’s lowest sovereign-risk markets.
  • Growing demand for recurring connectivity services: Mobile service revenues increased by 5.6% and fixed internet revenues by 5.8% in 2025, according to OSIPTEL. Postpaid and controlled-plan mobile subscriptions grew by 10.1%, highlighting an expanding market for recurring services and deeper customer relationships.
  • Expanding fiber adoption across the country: Fiber connections grew by approximately 21% in 2025, with growth exceeding 26% outside Lima and Callao. This expansion supports opportunities to combine mobile and home broadband services, improve customer retention and bring advanced connectivity to more communities.
  • A strong fit with Millicom’s capabilities: These market dynamics offer an attractive setting for Millicom to apply its regional scale, experience in convergent services and disciplined investment approach. Following completion, the Group would seek to translate this potential into profitable growth, stronger cash generation and lasting benefits for customers.
